pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Ask a subagent to stop its current work. This call returns without waiting for it to stop. You can continue a direct child's conversation later with send_message. Subagents it started will keep running.

agent_id.description: The id of an agent created under you: your direct child or a deeper descendant.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job: output since the previous read for stream jobs, or the result of a finished final-output job.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job finishes or the timeout expires; a timed-out wait leaves the job running. Defaults to false.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds with wait: true. Defaults to and is capped by configuration.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List subagents you started, with their ids, labels, and status. running means it is working; inactive means it is not currently working. You will be notified when a subagent finishes; there is no need to keep checking its status. Use send_message to continue the conversation.

scope.description: children (default) lists direct children, which accept send_message in any status. descendants lists the whole tree below you with each entry's parent session id and depth; entries deeper than 1 accept only interrupt_agent.

tools.name: list_mcp_resource_templates
tools.description: List parameterized resource URI templates from an MCP server.

cursor.description: Continuation cursor returned by this server.

tools.name: list_mcp_resources
tools.description: List resources available from an MCP server.

cursor.description: Continuation cursor returned by this server.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__click
tools.description: Clicks on the provided element

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

dblClick.description: Set to true for double clicks. Default is false.

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__close_page
tools.description: Closes the page by its index. The last open page cannot be closed.

pageId.description: The ID of the page to close. Call list_pages to list pages.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__drag
tools.description: Drag an element onto another element

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

from_uid.description: The uid of the element to drag

to_uid.description: The uid of the element to drop into

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__emulate
tools.description: Emulates various features on the target page.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

networkConditions.description: Throttle network. Omit to disable throttling.

cpuThrottlingRate.description: Represents the CPU slowdown factor. Omit or set the rate to 1 to disable throttling

geolocation.description: Geolocation (`<latitude>,<longitude>`) to emulate. Latitude between -90 and 90. Longitude between -180 and 180. Omit to clear the geolocation override.

userAgent.description: User agent to emulate. Set to empty string to clear the user agent override.

colorScheme.description: Emulate the dark or the light mode. Set to "auto" to reset to the default.

viewport.description: Emulate device viewports '<width>x<height>x<devicePixelRatio>[,mobile][,touch][,landscape]'. 'touch' and 'mobile' to emulate mobile devices. 'landscape' to emulate landscape mode.

extraHttpHeaders.description: Extra HTTP headers as a JSON string object, e.g. {"X-Custom": "value", "Authorization": "Bearer token"}. Headers are included into every HTTP request originating from the page and persist across navigations until cleared. Pass an empty string to clear all extra headers.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__evaluate_script
tools.description: Evaluate a JavaScript function inside the target page. Returns the response as JSON, so returned values have to be JSON-serializable.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

function.description:
A JavaScript function declaration to be executed by the tool in the target page.
Example without arguments: `() => document.title` or `async () => await fetch("example.com")`.
Example with arguments: `(el) => el.innerText`

args.description: An optional list of arguments to pass to the function.

items.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

filePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a file to save the script output to. If omitted, the output is returned inline.

dialogAction.description: Handle dialogs while execution. "accept", "dismiss", or string for response of window.prompt. Defaults to accept.

waitForStableDom.description: Whether to wait for the DOM to settle. Pass false if the script only reads data. Defaults to true.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__fill
tools.description: Type text into an input, text area or select an option from a <select> element.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

value.description: The value to fill in. "true" or "false" for checkboxes and toggles, "true" for radio buttons.

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__fill_form
tools.description: Fill out multiple form elements (inputs, selects, checkboxes, radios) at once. ALWAYS prefer this tool over multiple individual 'fill' or 'click' calls when interacting with forms. It is significantly faster, more reliable, and reduces turn count. Example: Fill username, password, and check "Remember Me" in one call.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

uid.description: The uid of the element to fill out

value.description: Value for the element. "true" or "false" for checkboxes and toggles, "true" for radio buttons.

elements.description: Elements from snapshot to fill out.

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__get_console_message
tools.description: Gets a console message by its ID. You can get all messages by calling list_console_messages.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

msgid.description: The msgid of a console message on the page from the listed console messages

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__get_css_styles
tools.description:
Retrieve matched CSS rules, inline styles, inherited styles, and cascade information for an element identified by its UID.
Use this tool to debug why specific CSS properties are applied, overridden, or conflicting. Results are paginated and return 10 rules per page by default; use pageIdx to page through the remaining rules. Requires a UID from take_snapshot.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

uid.description: The uid of the element on the page from the page content snapshot to inspect CSS styles for

pageSize.description: Maximum number of CSS rules to return per page. Defaults to 10.

pageIdx.description: Page number to return (0-based). Defaults to 0 (the first page).

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__get_network_request
tools.description: Gets a network request by an optional reqid, if omitted returns the currently selected request in the DevTools Network panel. Useful for inspecting request headers (including 'Cookie') and response headers (including 'Set-Cookie' and directives).

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

reqid.description: The reqid of the network request. If omitted returns the currently selected request in the DevTools Network panel.

requestFilePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a .network-request file to save the request body to. If omitted, the body is returned inline.

responseFilePath.description: The absolute or relative path to a .network-response file to save the response body to. If omitted, the body is returned inline.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__handle_dialog
tools.description: If a browser dialog was opened, use this command to handle it

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

action.description: Whether to dismiss or accept the dialog

promptText.description: Optional prompt text to enter into the dialog.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__hover
tools.description: Hover over the provided element

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__lighthouse_audit
tools.description: Get Lighthouse score and reports for accessibility, SEO, best practices, and agentic browsing. This excludes performance. For performance audits, run performance_start_trace

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

outputDirPath.description: Directory for reports. If omitted, uses temporary files.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__list_console_messages
tools.description: List all console messages for the target page since the last navigation.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of messages to return. When omitted, returns all messages.

pageIdx.description: Page number to return (0-based). When omitted, returns the first page.

types.description: Filter messages to only return messages of the specified resource types. When omitted or empty, returns all messages.

includePreservedMessages.description: Set to true to return the preserved messages over the last 3 navigations.

includeStackTraces.description: Set to true to include the stack trace for each message when available. Increases the response size.

serviceWorkerId.description: Filter messages to only return messages of the specified service worker.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__list_network_requests
tools.description: Lists the most recent requests for the target page since the last navigation.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

pageSize.description: Maximum number of requests to return. When omitted, returns all requests.

pageIdx.description: Page number to return (0-based). When omitted, returns the first page.

resourceTypes.description: Filter requests to only return requests of the specified resource types. When omitted or empty, returns all requests.

includePreservedRequests.description: Set to true to return the preserved requests over the last 3 navigations.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__list_pages
tools.description: Get a list of pages open in the browser.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__navigate_page
tools.description: Go to a URL, or back, forward, or reload. Use project URL if not specified otherwise.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

type.description: Navigate the page by URL, back or forward in history, or reload.

ignoreCache.description: Whether to ignore cache on reload.

handleBeforeUnload.description: Whether to auto accept or beforeunload dialogs triggered by this navigation. Default is accept.

initScript.description: A JavaScript script to be executed on each new document before any other scripts for the next navigation.

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. If set to 0, the default timeout will be used.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__new_page
tools.description: Open a new tab and load a URL. Use project URL if not specified otherwise.

url.description: URL to load in a new page.

background.description: Whether to open the page in the background without bringing it to the front. Default is false (foreground).

isolatedContext.description: If specified, the page is created in an isolated browser context with the given name. Pages in the same browser context share cookies and storage. Pages in different browser contexts are fully isolated (useful for clean-slate testing of cookies and authentication).

timeout.description: Maximum wait time in milliseconds. If set to 0, the default timeout will be used.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__performance_analyze_insight
tools.description: Provides more detailed information on a specific Performance Insight of an insight set that was highlighted in the results of a trace recording.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

insightSetId.description: The id for the specific insight set. Only use the ids given in the "Available insight sets" list.

insightName.description: The name of the Insight you want more information on. For example: "DocumentLatency" or "LCPBreakdown"

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__performance_start_trace
tools.description: Start a performance trace on the target webpage. Use to find frontend performance issues, Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS), and improve page load speed.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

reload.description: Determines if, once tracing has started, the target page should be automatically reloaded. Navigate the page to the right URL using the navigate_page tool BEFORE starting the trace if reload or autoStop is set to true.

filePath.description: The absolute file path, or a file path relative to the current working directory, to save the raw trace data. For example, trace.json.gz (compressed) or trace.json (uncompressed).

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__performance_stop_trace
tools.description: Stop the active performance trace recording on the target webpage.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

filePath.description: The absolute file path, or a file path relative to the current working directory, to save the raw trace data. For example, trace.json.gz (compressed) or trace.json (uncompressed).

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__press_key

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

key.description: A key or a combination (e.g., "Enter", "Control+A", "Control++", "Control+Shift+R"). Modifiers: Control, Shift, Alt, Meta

includeSnapshot.description: Whether to include a snapshot in the response. Default is false.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__resize_page
tools.description: Resizes the page's window so that the page has specified dimension

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__select_page

pageId.description: The ID of the page to select. Call list_pages to get available pages.

bringToFront.description: Whether to focus the page and bring it to the top.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

filePath.description: A path to a .heapsnapshot file to save the heapsnapshot to.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__take_screenshot
tools.description: Take a screenshot of the page or element.

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

format.description: Type of format to save the screenshot as. Default is "png"

quality.description: Compression quality for JPEG and WebP formats (0-100). Higher values mean better quality but larger file sizes. Ignored for PNG format.

uid.description: The uid of an element on the page from the page content snapshot. If omitted, takes a page screenshot.

fullPage.description: If set to true takes a screenshot of the full page instead of the currently visible viewport. Incompatible with uid.

filePath.description: The absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory, to save the screenshot to instead of attaching it to the response.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__take_snapshot
tools.description:

identifier (uid). Always use the latest snapshot. Prefer taking a snapshot over taking a screenshot. The snapshot indicates the element selected
in the DevTools Elements panel (if any).

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

verbose.description: Whether to include all possible information available in the full a11y tree. Default is false.

filePath.description: The absolute path, or a path relative to the current working directory, to save the snapshot to instead of attaching it to the response.

tools.name: mcp__chrome-devtools__type_text
tools.description: Type text using keyboard into a previously focused input

pageId.description: Targets a specific page by ID.

submitKey.description: Optional key to press after typing. E.g., "Enter", "Tab", "Escape"

tools.name: mcp__chrome__chrome_bookmark_add
tools.description: Add a new bookmark to Chrome

url.description: URL to bookmark. If not provided, uses the current active tab URL.

title.description: Title for the bookmark. If not provided, uses the page title from the URL.

tools.name: mcp__chrome__chrome_bookmark_delete

url.description: URL of the bookmark to delete. Used if bookmarkId is not provided.

title.description: Title of the bookmark to help with matching when deleting by URL.

tools.name: mcp__chrome__chrome_bookmark_search
tools.description: Search Chrome bookmarks by title and URL

query.description: Search query to match against bookmark titles and URLs. Leave empty to retrieve all bookmarks.

maxResults.description: Maximum number of bookmarks to return (default: 50)

folderPath.description: Optional folder path or ID to limit search to a specific bookmark folder. Can be a path string (e.g., "Work/Projects") or a folder ID.

tools.name: mcp__chrome__chrome_click_element
tools.description: Click on an element in a web page. Supports multiple targeting methods: CSS selector, XPath, element ref (from chrome_read_page), or viewport coordinates. More focused than chrome_computer for simple click operations.

selector.description: CSS selector or XPath for the element to click.

ref.description: Element ref from chrome_read_page (takes precedence over selector).

double.description: Perform double click when true (default: false).

modifiers.description: Modifier keys to hold during click.

waitForNavigation.description: Wait for navigation to complete after click (default: false).

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses the current active tab.

windowId.description: Window ID to select active tab from (when tabId is omitted).

frameId.description: Target frame ID for iframe support.

tools.description: Close one or more browser tabs

tabIds.description: Array of tab IDs to close. If not provided, will close the active tab.

url.description: Close tabs matching this URL. Can be used instead of tabIds.

tools.name: mcp__chrome__chrome_computer
tools.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a read_page to determine the ref of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try screenshot and then adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

background.description: Avoid focusing/activating tab/window for certain operations (best-effort). Default: false

action.description: Action to perform: left_click | right_click | double_click | triple_click | left_click_drag | scroll | scroll_to | type | key | fill | fill_form | hover | wait | resize_page | zoom | screenshot

ref.description: Element ref from chrome_read_page. For click/scroll/scroll_to/key/type and drag end when provided; takes precedence over coordinates.

coordinates.description: Coordinates for actions (in screenshot space if a recent screenshot was taken, otherwise viewport). Required for click/scroll and as end point for drag.

startRef.description: Drag start ref from chrome_read_page (alternative to startCoordinates).

scrollDirection.description: Scroll direction: up | down | left | right

text.description: Text to type (for action=type) or keys/chords separated by space (for action=key, e.g. "Backspace Enter" or "cmd+a")

repeat.description: For action=key: number of times to repeat the key sequence (integer 1-100, default 1).

region.description: For action=zoom: rectangular region to capture (x0,y0)-(x1,y1) in viewport pixels (or screenshot-space if a recent screenshot context exists).

selector.description: CSS selector for fill (alternative to ref).

value.description: Value to set for action=fill (string | boolean | number)

elements.description: For action=fill_form: list of elements to fill (ref + value)

appear.description: For action=wait with text: whether to wait for the text to appear (true, default) or disappear (false)

timeout.description: For action=wait with text: timeout in milliseconds (default 10000, max 120000)

tools.name: mcp__chrome__chrome_console
tools.description: Capture console output from a browser tab. Supports snapshot mode (default; one-time capture with ~2s wait) and buffer mode (persistent per-tab buffer you can read/clear instantly without waiting).

url.description: URL to navigate to and capture console from. If not provided, uses the current active tab

tabId.description: Target an existing tab by ID (default: active tab).

windowId.description: Target window ID to pick active tab when tabId is omitted.

background.description: Do not activate tab/focus window when capturing via CDP. Default: false

includeExceptions.description: Include uncaught exceptions in the output (default: true)

maxMessages.description: Maximum number of console messages to capture in snapshot mode (default: 100). If limit is provided, it takes precedence.

mode.description: Console capture mode: snapshot (default; waits ~2s for messages) or buffer (persistent per-tab buffer; reads from memory instantly).

clear.description: Buffer mode only: clear the buffered logs for this tab before reading (default: false). Use clearAfterRead instead to clear after reading (mcp-tools.js style).

clearAfterRead.description: Buffer mode only: clear the buffered logs for this tab AFTER reading, to avoid duplicate messages on subsequent calls (default: false). This matches mcp-tools.js behavior.

pattern.description: Optional regex filter applied to message/exception text. Supports /pattern/flags syntax.

onlyErrors.description: Only return error-level console messages (and exceptions when includeExceptions=true). Default: false.

limit.description: Limit returned console messages. In snapshot mode this is an alias for maxMessages; in buffer mode it limits returned messages from the buffer.

tools.name: mcp__chrome__chrome_fill_or_select
tools.description: Fill or select a form element on a web page. Supports input, textarea, select, checkbox, and radio elements. Use CSS selector, XPath, or element ref to target the element.

selector.description: CSS selector or XPath for the form element.

ref.description: Element ref from chrome_read_page (takes precedence over selector).

value.description: Value to fill. For text inputs: string. For checkboxes/radios: boolean. For selects: option value or text.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses the current active tab.

windowId.description: Window ID to select active tab from (when tabId is omitted).

frameId.description: Target frame ID for iframe support.

tools.name: mcp__chrome__chrome_get_web_content
tools.description: Fetch content from a web page

url.description: URL to fetch content from. If not provided, uses the current active tab

tabId.description: Target an existing tab by ID (default: active tab).

background.description: Do not activate tab/focus window while fetching (default: false)

htmlContent.description: Get the visible HTML content of the page. If true, textContent will be ignored (default: false)

textContent.description: Get the visible text content of the page with metadata. Ignored if htmlContent is true (default: true)

selector.description: CSS selector to get content from a specific element. If provided, only content from this element will be returned

tools.name: mcp__chrome__chrome_gif_recorder
tools.description:
Record browser tab activity as an animated GIF.

Modes:
- Fixed FPS mode (action="start"): Captures frames at regular intervals. Good for animations/videos.
- Auto-capture mode (action="auto_start"): Captures frames automatically when chrome_computer or chrome_navigate actions succeed. Better for interaction recordings with natural pacing.

Use "stop" to end recording and save the GIF.

action.description:
Action to perform:
- "start": Begin fixed-FPS recording (captures frames at regular intervals)
- "auto_start": Begin auto-capture mode (frames captured on tool actions)
- "stop": End recording and save GIF
- "status": Get current recording state
- "capture": Manually trigger a frame capture in auto mode
- "clear": Clear all recording state and cached GIF without saving
- "export": Export the last recorded GIF (download or drag&drop upload)

tabId.description: Target tab ID (default: active tab). Used with "start"/"auto_start" for recording, and with "export" (download=false) for drag&drop upload target.

fps.description: Frames per second for fixed-FPS mode (1-30, default: 5). Higher values = smoother but larger file.

durationMs.description: Maximum recording duration in milliseconds (default: 5000, max: 60000). Only for fixed-FPS mode.

maxFrames.description: Maximum number of frames to capture (default: 50 for fixed-FPS, 100 for auto mode, max: 300).

width.description: Output GIF width in pixels (default: 800, max: 1920).

height.description: Output GIF height in pixels (default: 600, max: 1080).

maxColors.description: Maximum colors in palette (default: 256). Lower values = smaller file size.

filename.description: Output filename (without extension). Defaults to timestamped name.

captureDelayMs.description: Auto-capture mode only: Delay in ms after action before capturing frame (default: 150). Allows UI to stabilize.

frameDelayCs.description: Auto-capture mode only: Display duration per frame in centiseconds (default: 20 = 200ms per frame).

annotation.description: Auto-capture mode only (action="capture"): Optional text label to render on the captured frame.

download.description: Export action only: Set to true (default) to download the GIF, or false to upload via drag&drop.

coordinates.description: Export action only (when download=false): Target coordinates for drag&drop upload.

ref.description: Export action only (when download=false): Element ref from chrome_read_page for drag&drop target.

selector.description: Export action only (when download=false): CSS selector for drag&drop target element.

enhancedRendering.description: Auto-capture mode only: Configure visual overlays for recorded actions (click indicators, drag paths, labels). Pass `true` to enable all defaults.

animationIntervalMs.description: Interval between animation frames in ms (default: 80)

clickIndicators.description: Click indicator overlay config (true for defaults, or object for custom).

dragPaths.description: Drag path overlay config (true for defaults, or object for custom).

labels.description: Action label overlay config (true for defaults, or object for custom).

durationMs.description: How long overlays remain visible in ms (default: 1500).

tools.name: mcp__chrome__chrome_handle_dialog
tools.description: Handle JavaScript dialogs (alert/confirm/prompt) via CDP

promptText.description: Optional prompt text when accepting a prompt

tools.name: mcp__chrome__chrome_handle_download
tools.description: Wait for a browser download and return details (id, filename, url, state, size)

filenameContains.description: Filter by substring in filename or URL

tools.name: mcp__chrome__chrome_history
tools.description: Retrieve and search browsing history from Chrome

text.description: Text to search for in history URLs and titles. Leave empty to retrieve all history entries within the time range.

startTime.description: Start time as a date string. Supports ISO format (e.g., "2023-10-01", "2023-10-01T14:30:00"), relative times (e.g., "1 day ago", "2 weeks ago", "3 months ago", "1 year ago"), and special keywords ("now", "today", "yesterday"). Default: 24 hours ago

endTime.description: End time as a date string. Supports ISO format (e.g., "2023-10-31", "2023-10-31T14:30:00"), relative times (e.g., "1 day ago", "2 weeks ago", "3 months ago", "1 year ago"), and special keywords ("now", "today", "yesterday"). Default: current time

maxResults.description: Maximum number of history entries to return. Use this to limit results for performance or to focus on the most relevant entries. (default: 100)

excludeCurrentTabs.description: When set to true, filters out URLs that are currently open in any browser tab. Useful for finding pages you've visited but don't have open anymore. (default: false)

tools.name: mcp__chrome__chrome_javascript
tools.description: Execute JavaScript code in a browser tab and return the result. Uses CDP Runtime.evaluate with awaitPromise and returnByValue; automatically falls back to chrome.scripting.executeScript if the debugger is busy. Output is sanitized (sensitive data redacted) and truncated by default.

code.description: JavaScript code to execute. Runs inside an async function body, so top-level await and "return ..." are supported.

tabId.description: Target tab ID. If omitted, uses the current active tab.

tools.name: pwsh
tools.description: Execute a PowerShell command (`pwsh -Command`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh pwsh process; pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Paths use native Windows form (`C:\...`); read environment variables with `$env:NAME`. Managed `$env:DSH_*` variables expose current harness environment facts. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. On Windows a force-killed command settles as `[exit code: 1]` without a signal marker — treat it as an interruption, not a command failure. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]`, a policy denial: do not retry another way. Under the Windows sandbox, read-only pwsh runs in PowerShell ConstrainedLanguage mode, while workspace-write stays in FullLanguage unless host policy says otherwise. In read-only, prefer cmdlets and core types (`[string]`, `[datetime]`, `[regex]`, `[guid]`); .NET static calls (`[System.IO.*]::`, `[math]::`), `Add-Type`, COM objects, and reflection fail with "only core types" errors. `-f` formatting, property access, and core cmdlets work. In both confined modes, programs cannot open named pipes, so a command that captures another program's output through piped stdio (Node.js `child_process.spawn`/`exec` with the default `stdio: 'pipe'`) fails with EPERM, while `stdio: 'inherit'` and `stdio: 'ignore'` spawns work and PowerShell's own pipelines are unaffected. That EPERM is the documented boundary: do not retry the command another way — escalate the exact command once or restructure it to avoid capturing output.

tools.name: workflow
tools.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.
